# The log {#sec-data} Before asking how the canvas behaves, we need to know exactly what was recorded. This chapter loads the log, looks at what one record is, lists what is odd about it, and draws the canvas from it. Nothing here is a finding about people yet; it is the ground the rest of the book stands on. ## One placement is one row ::: {#575061c9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import polars as pl import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import rplace17 as r d = r.load() # sorted by time; the 3 rows without coordinates are dropped (see below) d.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
shape: (5, 5)
t_ususer_idxycolor
i64i32i16i16i8
14901189355480004138645005042
14901189475150004138645085032
14901189596190004138645095042
14901189736890004138645095032
14901189852510004138645095022
``` ::: ::: Each row is one pixel placement: - `t_us`: the time, in microseconds since 1970 (UTC). The release records milliseconds. - `user_id`: who placed it. The release gives a hashed account id; we replaced each hash by a small integer. - `x`, `y`: where, with `(0, 0)` at the top left. - `color`: which of the 16 colours, as an index into the palette. ::: {#e527c1be .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} pal = r.palette() fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 0.9)) ax.imshow(r.palette_rgb()[None, :, :], aspect="auto") ax.set_xticks(range(16)); ax.set_yticks([]) ax.set_title("the 16 colours, by index") plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](01-data_files/figure-html/cell-3-output-1.png){} ::: ::: ::: {#72d47e41 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} n_rows, n_users = d.height, d["user_id"].n_unique() print(f"{n_rows:,} placements by {n_users:,} accounts") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 16,567,564 placements by 1,166,938 accounts ``` ::: ::: So there are 16\,567\,564 placements by 1\,166\,938 accounts, on average 14\.2 placements each. How that average hides a very uneven spread is the subject of @sec-actors. ## What is odd about the log A dataset should be checked before it is trusted. These checks compare the log with what the rules say should be possible. ::: {#c1de2422 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} full = r.load(drop_missing=False) dup = full.height - full.unique().height missing = full["x"].null_count() edge = d.filter((pl.col("x") == 1000) | (pl.col("y") == 1000)).height print(f"rows without coordinates: {missing}") print(f"exact duplicate rows: {dup}") print(f"x or y equal to 1000: {edge:,} (the canvas is 1000 x 1000, so 0..999)") print(f"x range {d['x'].min()}..{d['x'].max()}, y range {d['y'].min()}..{d['y'].max()}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` rows without coordinates: 3 exact duplicate rows: 304 x or y equal to 1000: 3,256 (the canvas is 1000 x 1000, so 0..999) x range 0..1000, y range 0..1000 ``` ::: ::: - **3 rows have no coordinates** or colour. They are dated weeks after the event; we drop them. - **304 rows are exact duplicates** (same time, account, pixel and colour). We keep them, because we cannot tell a logging artefact from a real double click. - **3\,256 rows sit at coordinate 1000**, one past the edge of a 1000 × 1000 canvas. We keep them and draw a 1001 × 1001 canvas. ## When it happened ::: {#413c303f .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} hourly = (d.with_columns(pl.from_epoch("t_us", time_unit="us").dt.truncate("1h").alias("hour")) .group_by("hour").len().sort("hour")) launch = hourly.filter(pl.col("len") > 10_000)["hour"].min() # the first hour with more than 10,000 placements assert hourly.filter(pl.col("hour") == launch)["hour"].dt.epoch("us")[0] == r.LAUNCH_US # = rplace17.LAUNCH end = hourly["hour"].max() pre = d.filter(pl.from_epoch("t_us", time_unit="us") < launch) print("launch hour:", launch, " last hour:", end) print(f"before launch: {pre.height:,} placements by {pre['user_id'].n_unique()} accounts") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` launch hour: 2017-03-31 17:00:00 last hour: 2017-04-03 16:00:00 before launch: 8,266 placements by 768 accounts ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-hourly .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3)) ax.plot(hourly["hour"], hourly["len"], lw=1.2) ax.axvline(launch, ls="--", color="grey") ax.set_yscale("log") ax.set_ylabel("placements per hour") plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Placements per hour. The dashed line is the launch hour (the first hour with more than 10,000 placements).](01-data_files/figure-html/fig-hourly-output-1.png){#fig-hourly} ::: ::: The crowd arrives on 2017\-03\-31 17:00 UTC and stays until the canvas closes on 2017\-04\-03. Before that there are 8\,266 placements by 768 accounts, spread over the previous ten days: most likely testing before launch. We keep them in the files, but later chapters start their clock at the launch hour (`rplace17.LAUNCH_US`). ## The canvas, drawn from the log The canvas at any moment is just each pixel's latest colour. `canvas_at` keeps, for every pixel, the last placement up to a time and paints it; pixels nobody touched stay white. ::: {#cell-fig-final .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 7)) ax.imshow(r.canvas_at(d)) ax.set_axis_off() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The canvas after the last placement, rebuilt from the log.](01-data_files/figure-html/fig-final-output-1.png){#fig-final} ::: ::: The same function, called at earlier times, shows the canvas filling in. ::: {#cell-fig-snapshots .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} t0 = r.LAUNCH_US fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(12, 3.3)) for ax, hours in zip(axes, [1, 6, 24, 48]): ax.imshow(r.canvas_at(d, t0 + hours * 3_600_000_000)) ax.set_title(f"+{hours} h"); ax.set_axis_off() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The canvas 1, 6, 24 and 48 hours after launch.](01-data_files/figure-html/fig-snapshots-output-1.png){#fig-snapshots} ::: ::: ## How much of the history survives ::: {#0eb3d420 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} touched = d.select("x", "y").unique().height print(f"pixels ever placed: {touched:,} of {1001 * 1001:,}") print(f"placements still visible at the end: at most {touched / n_rows:.1%} (one per pixel)") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` pixels ever placed: 998,779 of 1,002,001 placements still visible at the end: at most 6.0% (one per pixel) ``` ::: ::: Only one placement per pixel can be visible at the end, so at most 6\.0% of all placements survive into the final picture. The final image is the tip of the log; almost everything people did was later painted over. That is why the rest of the book works from the full sequence and not from snapshots.
